speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I'm Dr. Agent. I can see you're experiencing mental status changes; to help me understand what's happening, could you describe when these changes started and if you have any fever or recent head injuries? REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count, Comprehensive Metabolic Panel, Thyroid Function Tests.

speaker: Patient
text: 48-year-old female. The patient has been brought to the emergency room by her family due to altered mental status. The family mentions that she has been increasingly confused over the past few days. No recent head trauma or known drug use. The patient has a smoking history of 30 pack-years.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Mental status changes. I also have Increased confusion, Lethargy. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Gastroenteritis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: I appreciate that previous advice, but your symptoms of confusion and lethargy are not typical of simple gastroenteritis. To clarify the cause of your altered mental status, do you have a history of diabetes, liver disease, or kidney problems?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Patient has a history of hypertension, managed with medication. No other significant medical history is reported. Social history: Patient is a smoker with a 30 pack-year history. Drinks alcohol socially. No illicit drug use is reported.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the history; your smoking history is notable. Given your confusion and lethargy without significant metabolic risk factors yet, have you noticed any changes in your vision, speech, or coordination recently? REQUEST TEST: Arterial Blood Gas, Serum Osmolality, Urine Toxicology Screen.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Subdural Hematoma. While your labs are currently normal, your significant smoking history and new onset confusion/lethargy raise strong concern for a chronic subdural hematoma, which can present with altered mental status even without a distinct traumatic event. Please lie still while I order an urgent CT of your head to confirm this.
